rows.label: At least ten full-semester courses for the major
rows.note: Counts English courses (including those cross-listed with English) plus the courses on the category tables. Other departments' literary-study courses need approval and are not counted automatically.

rows.label: At least 30 credits in the major
Distribution: before 1800, after 1800, Global South, and the Americas
rows.note: One course may fill up to two categories. The five-course floor comes from the 15-credit minimum.

categories.label: Literatures in English of the Global South
Literatures in English of the Americas

rows.label: At least one Americas course on a named minority or Indigenous US literary tradition (Latina/o, Pacific Islander, and others)
rows.note: The board cannot tell which course covers which tradition, so check the course descriptions.

rows.label: Two 4000-level English seminars
rows.note: The board cannot tell a seminar from other 4000-level English courses; independent study (ENGL 4950, listed by Cornell with no seminar section) is left out, and the confirm row covers the rest.

rows.label: Confirm your two 4000-level ENGL courses are seminars, not tutorials or independent study
rows.note: The board counts 4000-level ENGL courses other than the honors tutorials ENGL 4930 and 4940 and independent study; check each one is a seminar, and that any cross-listed course is taught as one.

rows.label: Three courses linked by a shared topic, theme, period, genre, or approach
rows.note: Counts the number of courses only; the board cannot judge whether they form a coherent cluster (see the confirm row).

rows.label: Confirm the three cluster courses are related, with your advisor
Each major course needs a C or better, with no S/U grades
First-year writing seminars do not count toward the major; honors tutorials fill no other category
Non-English-department courses (at most three), transfer and study abroad courses need advisor or DUS approval; at most two non-Cornell courses per term
rows.note: Up to three outside-department literary-study courses (2000-level or above) may count with advisor approval; distribution use and transfer or study abroad work need DUS approval. Not counted automatically.
